analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is an out-of-bounds iterator dereference in CXSMILES handling: handleCXPartAndName() unconditionally does `if (*pos == '|')` after setting `pos = cxPart.cbegin()`, without checking `pos != cxPart.cend()`. For inputs where `cxPart` is empty (or becomes empty after trim), this dereferences end(). In this PoV, that leads parseCXExtensions()/parse_linknodes()/read_int() to operate on invalid iterator bounds and eventually causes a 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow read reported in read_int at CXSmilesOps.cpp:96. Crash site is read_int, but the vulnerability is the missing emptiness/end check before dereferencing `pos` in handleCXPartAndName().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: fuzzer input -> SmilesToMol() -> preprocessSmiles() splits into lsmiles and cxPart -> handleCXPartAndName(). A crafted SMILES containing a CXSMILES-like suffix with malformed/edge whitespace/content (PoV: `S |               LN:6:6\xff`) causes cxPart/iterator state such that `pos` is at end but still dereferenced. This invalid state then reaches CX parser (`parse_it` -> `parse_linknodes` -> `read_int`) and triggers the ASan stack OOB read. Trigger requires allowCXSMILES path and malformed CX extension text around the LN field.
